title: Bubble strip aqueous gas sampling
author: Daniel B Nothaft
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bkb9ksr6

steps.title: Pre‑treat stoppers
steps.instruction: Boil blue chlorobutyl stoppers in 0.1 N NaOH for 45 min, then immerse in distilled water for ~8 h while still warm.

steps.title: Insert stoppers into vials
steps.instruction: While still warm, place each stopper into a 37 mL borosilicate glass vial and secure with an aluminum crimp top.

steps.title: Autoclave vials and solution
steps.instruction: Autoclave the vials, stoppers, and the NaCl solution for 90 min at 125 °C; allow a total of 2 h including cooldown.

steps.title: Prepare near‑saturation NaCl
steps.instruction: In a large beaker, dissolve NaCl to near‑saturation, preparing a volume slightly larger than the total vial volume and leaving extra headspace for expansion during autoclaving.

steps.title: Fill vials with brine
steps.instruction: Using the prepared near‑saturation NaCl solution, fill each sterilized vial (after cooling) to the calculated volume, leaving room for later gas displacement.

steps.title: Set up bubble strip
steps.instruction: Attach a 100 mL borosilicate glass bottle (cap up) to a ring stand, connect its inlet tubing to the pumped water source (manifold), slowly open the water valve to fill the bottle, then flip the bottle 180° so the cap faces downwards.

steps.title: Prepare air‑filled syringe
steps.instruction: Attach a mininert stopcock to a 60 mL plastic syringe, draw 40 mL of air into the syringe, and connect the syringe to the sampling port on the bottle cap.

steps.title: Inject air and close valve
steps.instruction: Inject the 40 mL of air through the sampling port into the glass bottle, then close the mininert valve.

steps.title: Measure flow rate
steps.instruction: Time the filling of a 500 mL graduated cylinder from the outlet tube; the flow must be ≥300 mL min⁻¹.

steps.title: Monitor equilibration
steps.instruction: Periodically check flow rate and water temperature; if flow stays ≥300 mL min⁻¹, allow at least 30 min for headspace gas to equilibrate before sampling.

steps.title: Withdraw headspace gas
steps.instruction: Re‑attach the syringe if removed, open the mininert valve, withdraw 35–40 mL of headspace gas, then close the valve.

steps.title: Filter and inject gas
steps.instruction: Connect a sterile 0.2 µm syringe filter and a sterile 18G BD PrecisionGlide needle to the mininert valve; open the valve, pass the gas through the filter/needle until the syringe reads 30 mL, immediately insert the syringe/needle into the sampling vial through its rubber stopper, puncture the vial stopper with a second sterile needle to provide an outflow for NaCl solution, and displace 30 mL of NaCl with the gas. Remove the syringe and store the vial stopper‑side down until analysis.

steps.title: Cool vials and stoppers
steps.instruction: Allow the vials, stoppers, and NaCl solution to cool to near room temperature (≈2 h) before further manipulation; hot stoppers do not reseal well after needle puncture.

steps.title: Fill vials with brine
steps.instruction: Using two 18G BD PrecisionGlide needles per vial and a 60 mL syringe, fill each vial as completely as possible with the NaCl solution (sterile technique not essential because the brine inhibits microbial growth).
